A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RaM study. The main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–F are readable and matchable; the additional reference page in v3 does not indicate missing scientific material.

before.justification: v2 reports original Design-Bench experiments, metric-correlation analyses, ablations, and synthetic heavy-tailed-noise experiments in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains the original benchmark, correlation, ablation, and synthetic-noise results. Their retention from v2 does not change their status as original empirical results.

M1.justification: Section 3.3 and Algorithm 1 retain the same data augmentation, ranking-loss training, and output adaptation for gradient ascent. The model architecture, losses, and optimization procedure are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both evaluate Ant, D’Kitty, Superconductor, TF-Bind-8, and TF-Bind-10, alongside the same synthetic heavy-tailed-noise scenarios in Appendix C. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The twenty baselines in Table 2 and comparator sets in Figure 2, Table 3, and the appendix experiments are unchanged. The newly cited Kim et al. review is not an evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendix E retain the same training/validation split, training budgets, model sizes, 128-candidate evaluation budget, and percentile metrics. OOD-data construction and the synthetic-noise protocols are also unchanged.

E4.justification: The ranking-loss comparisons, augmentation and output-adaptation ablations, list-length sensitivity study, OOD diagnostics, and heavy-tailed-noise analyses in Appendices C and F are retained without revision.

E5.justification: Both versions specify eight seeds in Sections 3.1 and 4.1 and retain the same uncertainty reporting in the result tables. No run-count disclosure, uncertainty-estimation procedure, or significance test changes.

E6.justification: All main-text and appendix result entries and findings are unchanged. For example, Table 2 retains mean ranks of 2.7 for RaM-RankCosine and 2.2 for RaM-ListNet.

T1.justification: Theorem 1 and its proof, the AUPCC definition, Theorem 2 and its assumptions, and the mathematical material in Appendices B–D are unchanged, including the heavy-tailed-noise counterexample.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about MSE’s limitations, AUPCC’s alignment with offline optimization, and RaM’s performance. The claimed novelty and contribution scope are unchanged.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning order preservation, ranking-loss robustness, and output adaptation are unchanged. Appendix discussions of unresolved OOD theory, weaker median performance, model limitations, and list-length sensitivity are also retained.

D1.justification: The implementation links and technical disclosures in Section 4.1 and Appendix E remain unchanged, including preprocessing, hyperparameters, model selection, and baseline implementation sources.

R1.justification: v3 adds Kim et al. (2025), “Offline model-based optimization: Comprehensive review,” to the introduction, Section 2.1, Appendix A.1, and bibliography. This is a limited citation addition without substantive changes to research positioning.

P1.justification: v3 adds an acknowledgment thanking Yi-Xiao He, updates the arXiv version/date text, and corrects punctuation in two bibliographic author initials. The scientific narrative and section organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: Local paragraph wrapping and bibliography spacing/page breaks change. Figures 1–3, Tables 1–13, and Algorithm 1 retain their visual content and structure; the appendix pagination shifts without redesign.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly updates the background citation and acknowledgment, with minor bibliographic and layout edits. The method, theory, empirical evidence, explanations, limitations, and reproducibility information remain unchanged throughout the paper and appendices, establishing no meaningful net change in overall quality.
